benchmark.reason: The search and injection scoring logic AC_PERF_01 through AC_PERF_03 measure is unchanged since the v0.6.0 candidate, so the report below is carried forward as prior evidence measured on 6ba3354b, now five releases old, and is not a measurement of this SHA.
benchmark.environment: darwin arm64 (Apple M1 Pro); isolated home /tmp/mb-bench-cYCwcl
benchmark.knownUnmeasuredCost: AC_PERF_03's path has changed three times since the carried-forward number was measured, and none of it is measured by any gate: 0.6.3's per-call SHA-256 of the bundle (documented ~5-10 ms), 0.6.4's ack round trip with the waits re-split into a 3 s connect-plus-handshake budget and a 10 s compute budget, and 0.6.5's warming reply and relocated model cache. The carried-forward warm p95 of about 162 ms predates all three.
benchmark.coldFigureCaveat: The report's AC_PERF_03 cold p95 of about 2.3 s is not comparable to a real cold start. The benchmark runs in one isolated home whose model cache is already warm by the time the cold probe runs, so it measures a fresh fallback process against a warm cache. Live cold starts on a fresh plugin root were about 68 s before this fix, which is the gap #92 closes and which no AC_PERF number ever showed.
benchmark.thresholdChecks: 6/6 AC_PERF groups true against the thresholds predeclared in the report; every measured p95 landed at least an order of magnitude inside its budget except incremental sync (11.6s of a 120s budget) and peak sync RSS (931.3MB of 2048MB). No threshold was tuned.
benchmark.injectionYield: warm_injected_ratio 1 and cold_injected_ratio 1 with error_ratio 0, over the benchmark's synthetic corpus; conversation search reported error_ratio 0 and no_match_ratio 0.
benchmark.contractGate: test/benchmark-contract.test.mjs was re-run after this report was written and validates it against the /api/v2/graph-only transport set; scripts/benchmark.mjs also validates the same contract before writing the file.

injectDaemonIdentity.defect: #84, found while validating 0.6.2: the injection fast path could be served by a daemon that was not the installed plugin, so a hook could receive context computed by a different build.
injectDaemonIdentity.design: A handshake now settles identity before any computation: the hook and the daemon must agree on five fields, and a SHA-256 of the bundle binds the answer to the build that produced it. The design was reviewed by Codex before implementation, and an implementation review folded six further defects into the same PR.
injectDaemonIdentity.reviewProvenance: Both the design review and the implementation review were Codex passes arranged by this project; they are not an outside audit.
injectDaemonIdentity.behaviour: A mismatching, older or timing-out daemon falls back in-process and records daemon.reason and daemon.got rather than serving a foreign answer. Socket ownership uses an O_EXCL lock, reclaims dead sockets and non-socket files left by SIGKILL, does not intervene on EACCES, and supports retire handover with refusal from a non-installed root. Only a listener at the installed root is accepted, MEMEX_INJECT_DAEMON can force the path, and doctor reports inject-daemon judged against the installed root without its probe contaminating inject-output.

reacquisition.defect: #89, found while validating 0.6.3 on the user's live data root, not by any gate. Codex rotates one MCP server per session or thread. A server that found a live owner at start-up stopped looking, so when the owner exited the socket file stayed behind: later prompts connected to it, got ECONNREFUSED, and paid the cold in-process path with no process anywhere intending to repair it.
reacquisition.liveObservation: On the real data root the owner pid 75485 was gone at 13:56 with its socket file left behind, and the resulting cold path was measured at 69.8 s. This is a live field observation of v0.6.3, not an observation of these gates — the v0.6.3 receipt's green gates did not and could not surface it, because every daemon case there ran in isolated fixtures within a single process lifetime.
reacquisition.fix: A server that did not bind now keeps watching: a re-probe every 20 s (MEMEX_INJECT_DAEMON_REACQUIRE_MS, timer unref'd so the watch never keeps the MCP server alive) plus an opportunistic probe on each of its own MCP requests, rate-limited to one attempt per 2 s and never awaited, so a busy host reclaims in milliseconds instead of waiting out the interval. The reclaim decision itself is unchanged and now shared by both entry points: nothing listening is reclaimed through the existing dead-socket path, a live same-build owner is left to serve, an unidentified listener is left untouched, and a live foreign owner gets the existing retire request. Re-probe outcomes are silent; only a state change logs. An owner now also releases the socket on the way out — SIGTERM, SIGINT, stdin close or a plain exit unlink the socket and drop the bind lock idempotently if it is still ours, then re-raise the signal so installing the handlers cannot swallow the MCP server's SIGTERM. That turns an ordinary exit into ENOENT, a clean cold start, instead of the corpse that made the bug permanent.
reacquisition.hookClassification: The hook now names why a fast path was refused — absent (no socket), refused (stale file), handshake timeout, compute timeout or identity mismatch — and falls back immediately on the first two instead of guessing at the daemon's silence.
reacquisition.budgets: The 3 s budget now covers connect plus handshake only: the daemon answers the handshake with an ack carrying its identity before it computes, and the compute wait shares the daemon's own 10 s per-connection budget (MEMEX_INJECT_COMPUTE_TIMEOUT_MS for tests).
reacquisition.abandonedBundle: A bundle whose requesting hook has already fallen back is rolled back inside the transaction with status "abandoned", so no prepared recall receipt is left behind.
reacquisition.doctorStates: memex doctor reports inject-daemon as absent, stale (naming the servers waiting to reclaim), hung, ok or mismatch, and stale is a warning only when no candidate server exists. The candidate list counts live pids only, so a report cannot promise a reclaim on behalf of a process that is gone.
reacquisition.newState: Non-serving servers publish themselves under conversation-index/inject-daemon.candidates/<pid>.json. No schema change.
reacquisition.caseGrowth: test/inject-daemon-slice.test.mjs grew from 17 cases in 0.6.3 to 26 in 0.6.4, and to 29 in 0.6.5 for the warming reply; see embeddingCache.
reacquisition.newCoverage: The added cases drive real child processes rather than in-process doubles: a duplicate server reclaims the socket after the owner is SIGKILLed, and a separate case pushes the re-probe timer out to ten minutes so that only an MCP request can reclaim, then asserts both that the reclaim happened and that the handshake afterwards answers with the reclaimer's pid. Others cover the hook against a stale socket file returning reason "refused" with a fallback inside 3 s, and doctor's four states including a live candidate named with its interval and a candidate whose pid is gone.
reacquisition.liveReacquisition: NOT_PROVEN: reclaim by timer and by MCP request is proven against real child processes in isolated fixtures, but not against Codex's own server rotation on the user's root. Whether the 69.8 s cold path is actually gone in live use is verified after release.

injectDaemonIdentity.regressions: test/inject-daemon-slice.test.mjs, 26 cases. The original 17 from 0.6.3: rejection of a daemon with no handshake or any single differing field with via "fallback" plus daemon.reason, the fast path served and attributed on a match, a real daemon against a real hook so that a disagreement between the two files' identity computations surfaces as fallback, reclaim of sockets and non-socket files left by SIGKILL, EACCES non-intervention, live and stale bind locks, retire handover and non-installed-root refusal, the installed-root policy with MEMEX_INJECT_DAEMON, and doctor's three verdicts. One case asserts the mismatching daemon was never asked to compute at all.
injectDaemonIdentity.knownCost: The per-call SHA-256 of the bundle from 0.6.3 is documented at roughly 5-10 ms on the fast path, and 0.6.4 adds the ack round trip and re-splits the timeouts into a 3 s handshake and a 10 s compute budget. None of it is measured by any gate; see webUi.benchmark.knownUnmeasuredCost.
injectDaemonIdentity.liveDaemonTakeover: NOT_PROVEN: socket handover, reclaim and the installed-root policy were exercised in isolated fixtures. No live daemon on the user's own root was taken over or retired, which is verified after release.

reviewRemediation.source: The external code review of v0.5.2..v0.6.1 by Codex gpt-6-astra at low reasoning effort, which raised 22 findings numbered #59 to #80.
reviewRemediation.status: All 22 findings remain closed as of 0.6.3; 0.6.4 adds no review-finding work. #89 is a separate defect found after that review, while validating 0.6.3 live.

closedInThisRelease.verifiedFromChangelog: The 0.6.3 changelog body cites every one of these nine numbers; #79 and #80 appear together as (#79, #80). Its header writes the range (#59-#80), which is the review's extent.

reviewRemediation.arithmetic: 13 closed in 0.6.2 plus 9 closed here accounts for all 22.
reviewRemediation.regressions: The nine land across test/ontology-classifier.test.ts and test/ontology-taxonomy-repair.test.ts for the taxonomy epoch work (#73), test/capsule-size-truncation.test.ts for list-item caps (#85) and for the control-character scalar budget (#74), test/continuity-identity.test.ts, test/fact-tier-ladder.test.ts, test/injection-gate-observability.test.ts, test/recall-receipt-observability.test.ts, test/plugin-root-slice.test.mjs, test/lifecycle-slice.test.mjs, and the UI suites ui/test/core.cjs for audit-path pinning (#78) and ui/test/guidance.test.cjs for the model-call-failed versus model-invalid-json class (#79, #80).

testIsolationIncident.whenFound: During 0.6.3 development, by the isolation check introduced in 0.6.1. Recorded here as a carried-forward boundary; nothing leaked in this release's run.
testIsolationIncident.leak: The `taxonomy epoch vs privacy purge (P1/P2 v4)` block in test/ontology-classifier.test.ts set only TEST_DB_PATH. The #73 regressions call mergeCategories and renameCategory, which each append a metadata line to <getMemexHome()>/logs/ui-audit.jsonl, so getMemexHome() fell through to the user's real root and eight ontology-merge / ontology-rename rows landed in ~/.config/memex/logs/ui-audit.jsonl.
testIsolationIncident.scope: That one block was the only leak; test/ontology-taxonomy-repair.test.ts and test/ontology-cli-slice.test.mjs already pinned MEMEX_HOME.
testIsolationIncident.fix: The block now pins MEMEX_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to its temp directory and restores both afterwards. MEMEX_HOME alone decides getMemexHome(); XDG_CONFIG_HOME is pinned as well so the fallback cannot reach a real directory if that precedence ever changes. Both tests now also assert the audit line is readable under the temp home, so isolation is proven by the suite itself rather than only by the external check.
testIsolationIncident.thisGateResult: PASS again in this release: 126 files compared before and after the full run, 0 added, 0 removed, 0 modified.
testIsolationIncident.significance: This is the second leak of exactly this shape the check has caught; the first, in 0.5.0 QA, put 21 lines into the same file from test/web-ui-db-factory.test.mjs. The pattern is a suite isolating only a database path while a code path resolves the home directory independently.
testIsolationIncident.caveat: The eight leaked rows were written to the user's real audit log during development and are not removed by this fix; the check proves the gate run is clean now, not that the earlier write was undone.

embeddingCache.defect: #92, found while validating 0.6.4 on the user's live data root, not by any gate. @xenova/transformers defaults env.cacheDir to a path relative to the PACKAGE, <node_modules/@xenova/transformers>/.cache, and every Memex version unpacks into its own plugin root, so each update began with an empty cache.
embeddingCache.liveObservation: Measured on the real data root: the fresh 0.6.4 root downloaded 129 MB, and its first six inject runs took 69.6 s, 74.0 s, 69.8 s, 68.2 s, 68.6 s and 67.9 s, against 321-1,204 ms warm. A fresh per-session daemon also exceeded its 10 s compute budget on its first request while the hook's own fallback downloaded the same model concurrently. This is a live field observation of v0.6.4, not an observation of these gates.
embeddingCache.fix: src/model-cache.ts now owns the cache layout and the model id: weights live in <data root>/models, resolved through the same home precedence as the archive and the index, with MEMEX_MODEL_CACHE_DIR as the explicit override. env.cacheDir is assigned at module scope so it is set before any pipeline exists and re-applied in initEmbeddings so it follows a data root a harness moved after import; env.allowRemoteModels is unchanged. The module depends only on node builtins, paths.ts and plugin-root.ts — no model library — so doctor and the warm gate can answer whether the model is present on a host whose runtime closure is missing.
embeddingCache.legacyMigration: On first use a complete legacy per-root cache is copied once, never moved, searching the running root, then other versions under the Codex plugin cache, then the launcher root, and the copy is logged. The copy writes nothing outside the cache directory, is a no-op when a model is already there, refuses an incomplete legacy cache, and resumes a partial copy while preserving existing files.
embeddingCache.warming: A daemon still warming its model answers {type:"warming"} instead of spending the 10 s compute budget; the hook records reason "warming" and falls back at once with no recall receipt, and the 10 s budget itself is unchanged. Socket owners preload the model in the background right after binding, and identify carries a warming field that doctor treats as ok.
embeddingCache.operatorSurface: `memex deps warm` downloads and exercises the model once; `memex update` and `memex deps materialize` run it automatically when the cache is empty, with --no-warm to skip, MEMEX_WARM_TIMEOUT_MS to bound it, and failure as a warning rather than an error. `memex doctor` gains embedding-cache, reporting location, resolution source, model id, file count and size, warning with "Run: memex deps warm" when absent and telling an interrupted download apart from a complete one.
embeddingCache.regressions: test/model-cache.test.ts, 25 cases: cache resolution with MEMEX_MODEL_CACHE_DIR over the data-root rule, no node_modules in the path, relative and empty-string handling, the <cacheDir>/<org>/<name> layout, env.cacheDir injection with allowRemoteModels preserved, five presence states including an interrupted download and zero-byte weights, and the legacy copy's byte-identical source, nothing written outside the cache, idempotency, refusal of an incomplete legacy cache, cross-version search with the running root preferred, and partial-copy resume. Every case uses fake files and downloads no model. test/model-cache-slice.test.mjs, 17 cases: doctor's five embedding-cache states including via env and via data-root, diagnostics never creating the cache directory, the deps warm help guards, warm skipping an already-warm or stub cache and reporting a load failure, materialize running the warm step even when dependencies are complete with --no-warm honoured and a warm failure exiting 0, and the --no-warm flag in memex update --help. test/inject-daemon-slice.test.mjs grew from 26 to 29 cases for the warming reply and the hook's warming fallback.

gateCachePinning.rule: The gate pins the model cache to the checkout's own transformers cache, the pre-0.6.5 location a dev checkout already has, so nothing is downloaded, nothing is copied and the real data root is untouched. An explicit MEMEX_MODEL_CACHE_DIR from the caller still wins, so a test that means to exercise resolution is not overridden.
gateCachePinning.mechanism: vitest.config.ts env for the .ts suites; import './model-cache-pin.mjs' as a side effect for the .mjs suites.
gateCachePinning.verifiedHere: No models/ directory existed in the real root before or after the run, and the pinned checkout cache was byte-stable at 132,228 KB across 4 files before and after, so no gate downloaded or copied a model.
gateCachePinning.residualRisk: The pin is per-suite discipline, not an enforced boundary: a new suite that loads the model without the vitest env or the pin import would leak again. The real-root check would catch it only if that suite also left MEMEX_HOME on the real root.

embeddingCache.liveWarmStart: NOT_PROVEN: that a real update now warms the cache once and that the next prompts are warm rather than a 68 s cold start is verified after release on the user's own root. No gate measured an inject run against a real cache, and the gates deliberately never download the model at all.

realRootIsolation.mode: read-only; snapshot before the gates, compare after, as docs/VERIFICATION.md §4 now requires
realRootIsolation.volatileExclusions: run-locks/ and unix sockets are excluded by default because they exist only while something is running; --strict was not used.
realRootIsolation.motivation: 0.5.0 QA found test/web-ui-db-factory.test.mjs isolating only MEMEX_DB_PATH and appending 21 lines to the real logs/ui-audit.jsonl. That suite is now inside the widened mjs gate, and this run leaves the real root byte-identical.
realRootIsolation.caveat: This proves the gate run did not write to the root, not that the root is healthy. Judgement is by content hash, so a read-only access that only moves atime is correctly not a failure.
